newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals - Little changed, some enquiry seen.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals - Little changed, some enquiry seen.

text.p: Minor metals held little changed levels during the past week, though pockets of consumer enquiry were noted by traders despite the traditionally slow summer period.
"Its all very relaxed but there has been enough enquiry to keep us ticking over," one trader commented.
Cobalt held steady on forward demand, while vanadium firmed slightly on short-supply

Traders said cobalt was eyeing higher levels near-term as they believed that the recent downside pricing operation in Russian material has finished. "We may see a gentle firming in prices during August," one London trader said.
High grade material remained thin on the ground.

Producers Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo were believed to be producing low grade material. One source said that high grade material coming out of Congo's Gecamines was less than 200 tonnes a month as the country recovered from a seven-month civil war, while Zambia had stopped air freighting metal in to Europe.
"It looks like the supply line from Zambia is dry," one trader said.

Traders will await the outcome of the Defence National Stockpile Center meeting on Thursday. The meeting has been called to discuss how to sell stockpiled cobalt following the recent legal dispute with Minor Metals Inc.
Vanadium firmed on tight supply, good demand and production problems in China. Also, with New Zealand Steel re-lining one of its smelts in September raw material will remain tight.
The reline will take around two months and will have a major impact on vanadium availability, traders said. Antimony was showing few signs of shrugging off its summer torpor.
Steady consumption and low stocks may soon stir prices.
"I think the market is starting to bottom out and will eventually turn," a trader said.
Floods in China was doing little to hamper production or transportation of antimony, traders with sources close to the region said.
Elsewhere, the expected probe higher in cadmium failed to materialise amid the lack of strong consumer demand, while bismuth's recent fall levelled off in expectations of fresh consumer covering.
